Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 marked a period of significant advancement for Voltara Motors, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record total vehicle deliveries of 178,452 units, a 28% year-over-year increase; substantial expansion of our charging network with thousands of new stalls and rising utilization rates; meaningful improvements in electric vehicle range and efficiency across our lineup; aggressive cost reduction initiatives that drove margin expansion; strong growth in our energy business revenue and profitability; detailed delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 and beyond; and confident revenue guidance reflecting our scaling momentum. The launch of our Voltara Apex SUV has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image, with market share gains in key segments and fleet partnerships accelerating adoption.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue was $2.5 billion, representing a substantial 30% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 23.2%, driven by increased production efficiencies, favorable product mix, and the effectiveness of our cost reduction programs. Operating expenses totaled $650 million, and net income amounted to $180 million. We are in a strong financial position with $4.8 billion in cash reserves. We project $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion for Q4 revenue, with full-year 2025 guidance at $12.5 billion to $13.5 billion.

Let me expand on some of these highlights, starting with our total vehicle deliveries. In the quarter ended September 30, 2024, we achieved 178,452 units delivered, a robust 28% YoY increase from 139,200 units in Q3 2023 and 12% sequential growth from Q2's 159,380 units. This beat our guidance midpoint and was driven by our diversified portfolio. The Apex Prime Sedan, our volume leader, delivered 92,150 units, up 35% YoY, thanks to the Highland Refresh 2.0 with LFP packs from our CATL partnership. The Apex Summit SUV saw 56,780 units, up 22% YoY, boosted by 4680 structural cells enabling 420-mile range. Our Apex Titan Pickup ramped to 29,522 units, a 450% YoY surge with 800V architecture and gigacasting efficiencies.

Regionally, North America led with 98,200 units, up 32% on IRA incentives; Europe at 42,150 units, up 18% despite tariffs; China 28,102 units, up 25% via localized production; and rest of world 10,000 units, up 45%. This performance came amid global BEV sales growing just 15% YoY, with our premium segments outperforming through supply chain de-risking, production ramps to 2,200 vehicles per day, and demand levers like fast-charging demos.

Turning to delivery volume guidance by model for Q4, we're guiding 170,000 to 185,000 vehicles globally, a 12% to 22% sequential increase, positioning for full-year 2024 at 620,000 to 650,000 units, or 32% YoY growth. By model: Apex Sedan 68,000 to 73,000 units, up 10-18% QoQ, with FY2025 at 280,000-310,000; Horizon SUV, our mid-size crossover, 76,000-82,000, FY2025 300,000-330,000; Titan Pickup 21,000-24,000, FY2025 90,000-110,000; and new Quantum Crossover launch at 4,500-6,000 units. Mix shifts to higher-ASP vehicles, NA at 52%, with tailwinds like IRA credits and cell cost-downs to $52/kWh.

This ties into our broader revenue guidance for Q4 2024 at $2.6-2.8 billion, 28% YoY growth at midpoint and 15% sequential from Q3's $2.3 billion estimate, with automotive at 92%. Vehicle deliveries guide to 55,000-60,000 units, ASP $48,000-50,000 on premium mix and Level 3 ADAS. NA $1.7 billion, Europe $650 million despite subsidy phase-outs, APAC $260 million. Gross margins to 22.5%, on 15% battery cost declines and 800V integration. For FY2025, $12.5-13.5 billion, 45% over 2024's $8.6 billion, with Georgia Phase 2 capacity, Apex Bolt pickup launch, and $500 million in FSD recurring revenue.

A major driver is our charging network expansion and utilization rates. We've deployed 4,200 new DC fast-charging stalls across 850 sites in Q3, bringing global total to 52,000—a 28% YoY and 8% sequential increase, including 1,800 in NA, 1,500 Europe, 900 APAC, with 65% V4 350kW-capable. Ahead of 75,000 by YE24 on $450 million capex, up 35%. NACS retrofits on 2,500 stalls unlock 15% roaming revenue; Europe IONNA co-locations for AFIR compliance. Utilization averaged 31.5%, up 420bps QoQ and 650bps YoY, generating $2.8 million revenue at $620 ARPU per stall, outpacing Electrify America. Drivers: OTA routing for 72% of vehicles, fleet deals with Ryder/Penske at 15% fill, AI load balancing at 99.2% uptime. 3-year payback at $110k capex per stall via in-house manufacturing; V2G added $1.2 million. Expect 35-38% utilization YE24 on IRA credits, despite permitting delays.

Our energy business also shone, with Q3 revenue at $1.45 billion, up 162% YoY and 28% QoQ—sixth straight triple-digit quarter. Gross profit $425 million at 29.3% margin, up 720bps; EBITDA $285 million at 19.7%. FY guide $6.2-6.8 billion, 140% growth, to 25% of total revenue. Megapack utility storage 68% at $985 million, 3.2 GWh deployed; Powerwall $320 million, 145,000 units; charging $145 million, 1,200 stalls. NA 62%, Europe 22%, APAC 16%, boosted by IRA $120 million credits, Lathrop at 40 GWh run-rate. Scale at 75% utilization, 85% in-house cells, Autobidder trades unlock leverage. $2 billion 2025 capex doubles Megapack to 160 GWh.

Cost reduction initiatives were highly effective, delivering 18% YoY COGS cut toward $35,000 breakeven. Manufacturing 45% of savings: unboxed process at 85% OEE, gigacasting replaces 70 parts, recycled aluminum. Supply chain 30%: lithium at $12k/tonne, vendor base to 850. Battery 20%: $88/kWh packs, 60% LFP, CTP 3.0. Overhead 5%. COGS $28,500, margins 22.1% up 520bps, FCF $1.1 billion YTD.

These underpin our strong position heading into Q4.

Next, Dr. Liam Chen will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes and reduced manufacturing costs, with Fremont and Spartanburg hitting high OEE through gigacasting and unboxed processes, directly supporting our 178,000+ deliveries and cost savings. Gigafactories in Georgia, Texas, and Berlin are ramping, with automation and cobots keeping headcount flat amid volume growth.

After me, we'll hear from Sophia Grant regarding our technological advancements.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We've achieved 18% YoY EPA range improvements fleet-wide, to 425 miles on Apex S with 102 kWh NMC 811 silicon-graphene cells at 285 Wh/kg; efficiency to 238 Wh/mi via 0.23 Cd aero, 97.5% motors, 800V charging in 18 minutes, OTA regen boosting 22%. Piloting 4680 cells, solid-state for 2027. Regional wins: 680 km WLTP in Europe, CLTC 450 km China. Battery costs to $85/kWh, margins to 28.4%. V2H/V2G in 85% fleet unlocks $50 million grid revenue by FY26. We're committed to developing cutting-edge solutions that will shape the future of mobility.

Following Sophia, Raj Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure the reliable flow of materials. Our focus on diversification and strategic partnerships has strengthened our supply chain resilience, securing 150 GWh cells through 2026 from Panasonic, LG, CATL; JVs for lithium, nickel recycling; phosphor in-house. Vendor consolidation, AI MRP at 95% accuracy cut inventory $280 million. Localized production dodges tariffs, with IRA content at 75%. This de-risked 95% on-time deliveries, supporting ramps amid volatility.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex for the Q&A session.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you. Operator, we're ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee at Goldman Sachs.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the charging network, can you elaborate on utilization trends and how NACS adoption is impacting roaming revenue?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, Jordan. Our Q3 fleet-wide utilization hit 31.5%, up 420bps QoQ, driven by software optimizations directing 72% of Voltara vehicles to nearby stalls, cutting wait times to 3.2 minutes. Dynamic pricing surges 20-30% peaks, fleet partnerships fill 15%, AI balancing ensures 99.2% uptime. NACS retrofits on 2,500 stalls unlocked 15% throughput from non-Voltara EVs, boosting ARPU to $620. Europe at 22%, China 18% premium focus; expect 35-38% YE24 as EV share hits 15%.

Operator:
Next question from Sarah Kim at Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Kim:
Great, thanks. For revenue guidance, how does the Q4 midpoint bake in mix shifts and regional dynamics?

Marcus Hale:
Sure, Sarah. The $2.6-2.8 billion midpoint assumes 92% from autos, 55-60k deliveries, ASP $48-50k on Apex Max SUV and Pulse sedan ramps. NA 65% mix at $1.7B on IRA/Hertz wins; Europe 25% $650M tempered by subsidies but Berlin 4680 aids margins; APAC 10%. FY25 $12.5-13.5B on capacity adds, Bolt pickup, FSD $500M. Risks like lithium volatility offset by cost-outs.

Operator:
Next from Mike Torres at JPMorgan.

Mike Torres:
Thanks. Liam, on manufacturing, how effective were gigacasting and unboxed in cost reductions?

Dr. Liam Chen:
Mike, spot on—these were 45% of our 18% YoY COGS cut. 9,000-ton presses replace 70 stampings/300 welds, cycle to 22 seconds, OEE 85%. Recycled aluminum at 40%, IRA credits $120/kWh. Spartanburg 4680 ramp drops powertrain $350/unit; Munich localizes 60%. Utilization 92%, Wright's Law shaves 18% per doubling.

Operator:
Next from Emily Chen at Barclays.

Emily Chen:
Thanks. Sophia, details on range/efficiency gains and battery roadmap?

Sophia Grant:
Emily, fleet EPA range up 18% YoY, Apex S 425 miles on 102 kWh 285 Wh/kg cells; 238 Wh/mi efficiency beats Tesla Model Y. Aero 0.23 Cd, 800V 18-min charges, OTA regen +22%, preconditioning -15% HVAC. 4680 pilots cut cooling 8%; Samsung solid-state for 500 miles/200 Wh/mi 2027. Ecosystem V2G $50M FY26.

Operator:
Next from David Wong at Citi.

David Wong:
Appreciate it. Raj, supply chain risks and charging synergies?

Raj Patel:
David, diversification via 150 GWh offtakes, Australian lithium JV at $12k/tonne hedges volatility. Vendor to 850, AI 95% forecast saves $280M inventory. Charging ties in: Shanghai adds 300 stalls, NACS roaming 15%; IONNA co-locates 1,200. De-risks for 25% utilization China Q4.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Lisa Patel at RBC Capital.

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, team. Elena, big picture on energy business profitability and FY guide?

Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, energy at $1.45B Q3 revenue, 29.3% gross/19.7% EBITDA, up massively. Megapack 3.2 GWh, Powerwall 145k units + VPP $45M, charging 1,200 stalls. IRA $120M boost, Lathrop $55/kWh cells. FY $6.2-6.8B at 30-32% margins, 25% of total revenue. $2B capex doubles capacity; Autobidder, Energy OS position for $500B TAM.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
